hook: The James Webb Space Telescope detected water and cosmic dust just 0.55 light-years from Sagittarius A*.

sections.voiceover: The James Webb Space Telescope detected water and cosmic dust just 0.55 light-years from Sagittarius A*.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic deep space visualization zooming into the bright galactic core of the Milky Way towards supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep space hum with low bass swell

sections.voiceover: Astronomers observed star IRS 3 located 26,000 light-years from Earth. That star sits 0.55 light-years from supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*. How can molecules survive near Sagittarius A*?
sections.visual_cue: Telescope view of star IRS 3 near the center of the Milky Way, displaying orbital distance measurement markers.

sections.voiceover: However, studies at Universität zu Köln reveal star IRS 3 maintains an exceptionally large envelope.
sections.visual_cue: Detailed scientific diagram of star IRS 3 expanding a massive gas shell near the central galactic environment.

sections.voiceover: Universität zu Köln researchers found star IRS 3 actively emits gas and dust.
sections.visual_cue: Infrared animation of gas emissions shielding water vapor surrounding IRS 3 from intense central black hole radiation.

sections.voiceover: Researchers used the James Webb Space Telescope to detect water around aging star IRS 3.
sections.visual_cue: Wide view of the James Webb Space Telescope facing the glowing center of the Milky Way galaxy.
b_roll: James Webb Space Telescope in orbit
